messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: OTLP/Honeycomb exporter errors detected. Multiple services reporting 429s to honeycomb.us; traces dropping. Paging SRE on-call.

Alex M: oncall here, picking this up. Which services are affected? any customer-facing impact?

Sara P: looks like the otel-collector -> honeycomb exporter is hitting strict rate limits. Stack: otel-collector (k8s) using honeycomb OTLP/HTTP. Errors in logs show repeated 429 + Retry-After. Affected clusters: eu-west-1 and us-east-1 tracing pipelines.

Sara P: paste of recent log snippet:
```
2026-03-18T08:12:03Z exporter/honeycomb: export failed: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests (x-request-id=abc123)
2026-03-18T08:12:03Z exporter/honeycomb: response body: {"message":"rate limit exceeded","retry_after":45}
2026-03-18T08:12:07Z exporter/honeycomb: queuing span bundle, queue_len=12432
```

Alex M: thanks. impact? are alerts firing?

ops-bot: Alert: trace-drop-rate > 5% for service=runtime-proxy (eu-west-1) — triggered 2m ago.

Sara P: Alerting still functional (metrics/logs), only tracing is degraded. This is causing ~30% of spans dropped for sampled traces in affected regions. No inference customer requests failing. Primary concern: loss of distributed tracing and debugability; also retrospective reingest backlog growing.

Alex M: okay, mitigation plan options: 1) toggle local buffering to disk and increase max_queue; 2) switch exporter to our secondary sink (s3-archive) to persist raw OTLP and reingest later; 3) ask Honeycomb to lift throttle or increase quota for short window. I'll take 1 and 2 in parallel. Jamal please coordinate Honeycomb contact.

Jamal R: on it. creating support case now. Can someone grab earliest failing request IDs and sample traces? Need correlation IDs for Honeycomb.

Sara P: grabbing IDs now — added examples to the ticket. Also preparing a k8s patch to enable file buffer and bump worker concurrency on the otel-collector. Patch (kubectl patch command):
```
kubectl -n observability patch deployment otel-collector --patch '\n{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"otel-collector","env":[{"name":"OTEL_EXPORTER_HNY_MAX_QUEUE","value":"20000"},{"name":"OTEL_EXPORTER_HNY_BUFFER_DIR","value":"/var/otel-buffer"}] }] } } }'
```

Alex M: before applying, what's disk usage on collectors? we can't exhaust nodes.

Sara P: current disk usage on collectors < 45%. Buffer dir default is 10GB. We'll set buffer_dir to mount at /data/otel-buffer with a 50GB ephemeral volume. Applying patch in canary (eu-west-1a) first.

Emily (support): I'll draft customer-facing note that traces may be incomplete for recent window — will confirm exact times as we have them. Do we want to inform any customers proactively?

Alex M: let's hold on external comms until we confirm extent. Notify account owners for customers with high trace dependency (listed in alert runbook).

Jamal R: Honeycomb support case created: CASE-2026-03-18-9881. Contacted support via portal and attached logs. They responded with: "We're seeing ingestion throttling for your Team Key due to burst pattern from our collector; our mitigation is to advise reducing burst size or enabling our streaming ingest. We can temporarily increase limit for 1 hour upon request."

Sara P: we also have immediate toggle: enable alternate exporter to S3 (internal archive) — this requires flipping feature flag in observability-config. Command to flip using our config service (dry-run shown):
```
curl -X POST https://config.internal/api/v1/flags/observability/enable_s3_export 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 
 -d '{"value":true, "reason":"honeycomb-throttle-2026-03-18"}'
```

Alex M: do it. set to true and apply collector config to start writing to s3-archive. We'll reingest when Honeycomb confirms receipts are complete.

Sara P: flag enabled, applying collector restart to pick up new exporter. Rolling restart in progress for collectors in eu-west-1 canary.

ops-bot: Deployment otel-collector-eu-west-1a restart started (uid=deploy-789).

Sara P: canary done, exporter now writing to s3-archive. queue_len on canary fell from 12k -> 0 as items persisted to S3 backend. Monitoring canary for 5m.

Honeycomb Support: We can temporarily lift throttle for team-key=redwood-prod for 60 minutes to catch up; please provide expected burst and desired window.

Jamal R: requested 60m lift starting now + asked for details on backpressure causes. Also asked for upstream guidance about batching settings.

Alex M: good — we'll coordinate with Honeycomb to re-enable direct exporter after we drain backlog in S3 and confirm stability. Leave collectors writing to both sinks but prefer S3 as primary during catch-up? Sara, thoughts?

Sara P: dual-writing for now: still send to honeycomb but with stricter batching (max_export_batch_size=256 -> 64) and increased retry backoff. That reduces burst. Config snippet we applied:
```
exporters:
  honeycomb:
    max_batch_size: 64
    timeout: 30s
    retry_on_failure: true
    max_queue_size: 20000
```

Alex M: status update: canary looks good. Starting rolling restart for collectors in other AZs. Informing on-call infra to watch node disk.

ops-bot: Rolling restart initiated across 6 collector pods (eu-west-1). Progress: 2/6 restarted.

Sara P: Honeycomb confirmed throttle lifted. We're seeing 200 responses again (no more 429s) in canary and a slow decline of backlog. I'll start a controlled re-enable of direct export in us-east after 15m observation.

Emily (support): drafted internal incident note for account teams. ETA for final customer comms once we have exact window for dropped traces.

Alex M: handing to Jamal for follow-up and postmortem. Jamal, please capture timeline, root cause (burst pattern + batching defaults + Honeycomb rate limit), mitigation steps and a plan (tune batching defaults, enable persistent local buffer, consider self-managed streaming ingest, and run chaos tests for burst patterns). Classify as Sev2 (observability loss).

Jamal R: taking it. Will assemble timeline and assign owner for runbook updates. Also will request quota review with Honeycomb to formalize improved limits or streaming ingest.

Sara P: quick note for postmortem: include the exact collector image tag and config versions so we can reproduce. I saved them: otel-collector:v0.64.0-build-20260304, config v3.2.

Honeycomb Support: CASE-2026-03-18-9881 resolved: throttle lifted and we recommend staggered restarts and reduced batch sizes to avoid future bursts. Follow-up from Honeycomb PM scheduled.

Alex M: :white_check_mark: issue mitigated for now. We'll keep the S3 archive on until reingestion completes. Postmortem to follow. Closing pager for SRE team.

ops-bot: Pager resolved by user Alex M at 2026-03-18T12:09:03Z (runbook: observability/exporter-honeycomb).

Jamal R: postmortem draft comments: "Root cause: collector burst behavior combined with Honeycomb ingestion throttle and tight retry semantics. Action items: change default batch size to 64, enable disk buffering by default with 20GB minimum, add automated canary that simulates burst with production sampling, formalize a support SLA with Honeycomb for quota increases."

Emily (support): I'll schedule outbound comms template and coordinate with account owners to send tailored notes.

Alex M: thanks everyone. if anything regresses ping me directly.
